results: Added internal/bundles/activate.go with ActivationManager, ActivationStore, StorageActivationStore, ActivationRecord, ActivationRequest/Result/State and typed lifecycle error codes.
Activation reuses the C11 verifyAt gate (trust evidence, digest, Ed25519 signature, validity window, monotonic revision) and the policy BundleEvaluator structural validation before any durable write.

The verified record is committed as one atomic storage.WriteRecord (policyhelix:active-policy-bundle, owner_scope policyhelix, classification private); the manager then reads it back and confirms operation id, digest and highest revision before installing in-memory authority.

Restore reloads the durable record, revalidates signature, structure and freshness, exposes the previous bundle and highest accepted revision, and blocks activation when the record is corrupt or unreadable.

Interrupted switches at the staged-byte and manifest boundaries leave the previous bundle and revision 3 active; after storage reopen, Restore exposes only revision 3, evaluation still authorizes the operator, and one retry completes the switch at revision 4 and storage revision 2.

Retrying an already committed operation after a lost ACK returns status replayed with durable=true and performs no second commit; a delayed old operation is rejected as stale and cannot overwrite newer authority; reusing an operation id with different content is rejected as OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT.
A simulated read-back failure after the manifest rename returns ACTIVATION_COMMIT_UNCONFIRMED, and a restart exposes the complete new revision 3 while the same operation replays idempotently.

Disk-full and oversized-payload attempts return typed non-durable rejections, make exactly one commit attempt per call, leave the manifest and highest revision unchanged, and permit exactly one revision advance on a later retry.

Unauthenticated identities and authenticated subjects without operator/admin roles are rejected before any durable write; evaluation without authority, with unauthenticated private access, or after durable-record tampering denies with NO_ACTIVE_POLICY_BUNDLE or PRIVATE_RESOURCE_FAIL_CLOSED.

Exposed the typed outcome through engine CLI --activate-bundle and --activation-state with explicit trusted keys and storage directory; no non-loopback or unauthenticated activation surface was added.
Keyring.NewEvaluator now supplies the trusted issuer/signer sets to both BundleAuthorityManager and ActivationManager, preserving existing ingestion behavior.

tests/activation_test.go covers both crash boundaries, replay, lost ACK, read-back failure, disk full, bounded payload, private fail-closed, corrupt durable state, all ten fixtures and the CLI workflow; ten Apache-2.0 synthetic C12 fixtures are hash-verified through manifest.json.
observed_limitations: The activation record is bounded by the C05 64 KiB storage payload limit; a bundle near the policy bundle size bound cannot be persisted because the record wrapper exceeds the limit, and fails closed with PAYLOAD_TOO_LARGE instead of truncating.
Trust anchors are supplied by the CLI envelope per invocation; persistent trust-anchor configuration and OIDC login are C13/C14 scope.

If the manifest rename succeeds but the read-back fails, the live process keeps the previously restored authority until an explicit Restore or a same-operation retry; the durable record is already the complete new state and a restart exposes it.
Activation is exposed through the engine CLI only. The browser workspace and loopback HTTP surface do not display activation until storage lifecycle and configuration ownership are defined.

Crash coverage uses the deterministic C05 fault injection at the staged-byte and manifest boundaries plus close/reopen, which leaves the identical on-disk state as a killed writer at those boundaries; it does not SIGKILL an OS process mid-syscall.

Durable activation records already written under the C05 storage directory remain valid and digest-verified; a previous engine has no reader for policyhelix:active-policy-bundle but does not overwrite it. Keep the latest valid record and use a compatible reader for forward repair; never overwrite a newer accepted revision with an older backup.
